title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of quiescent epimastigotes as a resource for investigating the persister phenotype in Trypanosoma cruzi.
projectDescription: The “persister” phenotype is often associated with treatment failure. Our knowledge of parasite biology, in particular the mechanistic processes associated with persistence phenotype is limited The ability to isolate homogenous populations of dormant or slowly replicating parasites vs non-perturbed parasites is the limiting step in defining these phenotypes  In this context, the project implemented: The use of “fluorescent timer” proteins and live cell sorting as a method for isolating populations of non-perturbed slow-growing or dormant parasites Proteomics and transcriptomics methods, including a common sample collection/sample preparation procedure, from the parasites coming from the sorting to assess the mechanistic processes associated with parasite persistence The aim is the descritpion and to identify discriminant markers/pathways associated with parasite persistence
sampleProcessingProtocol: Paris lysates were mixed with equal volume of SP3 Lysis buffer (Preomics GmbH) in Covaris AFA tube. After ultrasonication on a M220 Series for 90 seconds at 75 W, 20.3% duty factor, 200 burst per cycle following by boiling at 95°C. Denatured extract was digested by SP3-iST kit (Preomics Gmbh). Peptides yield was determined using BCA kit (Thermo Scientific).  Mass spectrometry analysis Peptide analysis was performed on the Ultimate 3500 RS nano LC system coupled to the Exploris 480 mass spectrometer. 350 ng of peptide extracts were injected for each sample. Peptide were separated by 25 cm EasySpray column (75 µm internal diameter, particle size 2 µm) at a flow rate of 300 nl.min-1. After an isocratic step at 2% of solvent B over 3 min, the gradient consisted of a first increase of solvent B from 2% to 27.5% over 99 min, then from 22% to 40% over 5 min. Total run time, including column wash and re-equilibration, was 125 min. Tandem mass spectrometry analysis was performed on the Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) equipped with an Easy-Spray nanoprobe. The data independent acquisition (DIA) method consisted of a full scan acquired at a resolution of 120,000 from 375 and 1500 m/z (mass to charge ratio) (automatic gain control (AGC) target of 3*106 ions or 50 ms maximal injection time) and of 75 DIA windows (isolation 8 m/z, overlap 1 m/z) acquired at 30,000 from 400 to 1008 m/z.
dataProcessingProtocol: Extraction and annotation of proteomics MS spectra was performed using DIA-NN (v. 1.8) [26] software and Biotracs, an in-house workflow developed with MATLAB (R2021). The DIA-NN spectral library was generated using the proteomes of Homo sapiens (id: 9606, downloaded from Uniprot in February 2023) and Trypanosoma cruzi (id: 5693, downloaded from Uniprot in April 2023). Trypsin was specified as the enzyme, cleaving after all lysine and arginine residues, and allowing up to two missed cleavages. The N-terminal methionine excision was enabled. Carbamidomethylation of cysteine (+57.021 Da) was specified as a fixed modification and oxidation of methionine (+15.995 Da) and was considered as a variable modification. A False Discovery Rate (FDR) of less than 1% was applied to both peptide spectral matches and protein-based on linear discriminant analysis using a target decoy strategy. The resulting feature table was used for QC analysis, excluding proteins from the Homo sapiens database. Robust features present in over 80% of samples per group were retained. Missing features were gap-filled with values from a normal distribution around 1.104. Normalization was performed using the maxLFQ method in DIA-NN [27].
